answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016; stride 20):

- Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, covering 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping context: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED estimate (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated probability, using the LBNL catalogue):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198       5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922        0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474         0.0006484                        0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) probabilities of a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 earthquake are very low — 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year depending on the b scenario (b = 1.0, 0.73, 0.65), with Sigma around -5.3 to -5.4 (strongly sub-critical, no significant induced-seismicity anomaly). The DAS-based number (P = 0.07842/yr at b = 0.9849) is an upper bound only, because the DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are counted as events above Mc, which over-counts; it should not be read as a calibrated hazard probability.
